mainTopic: The altar ramps, where קמיצה and other services may be done (עזרה versus היכל), and the uses of the southwest corner of the מזבח
overview: This amud opens with רמי בר חמא's measurement: the main ramp of the מזבח was a little less steep than the small ramps. A new משנה then teaches that the קמיצה of a מנחה may be done anywhere in the עזרה, and that male כהנים eat the rest inside the courtyard until midnight. רבי אלעזר adds that a קמיצה done in the היכל is also valid, learning it from the removal of the בזיכין. רבי ירמיה challenges him from the פסוק 'וקמץ משם'. The answer is that the פסוק only comes to make the whole עזרה valid. The גמרא then works out why that פסוק was needed at all: comparisons to the north-side animal offerings all fail, so the real worry was that the קמיצה might be tied to the southwest corner, like the הגשה. Next, רבי יוחנן rules that שלמים slaughtered in the היכל are valid, because the less holy place should not be stricter than the holier one. The גמרא defends this logic: it works for service, but not for eating. A final משנה lists the six rites done at the southwest corner of the מזבח and begins the rule that everyone goes up the ramp on the right side. That rule continues on the next amud.

steps.title: How steep the altar ramps were
steps.stepSummary: רמי בר חמא gives the slope of the small ramps, and a gentler slope for the main ramp of the מזבח.
steps.simpleTranslation: רמי בר חמא says: each of the small ramps rose one cubit for every three cubits of length. The main ramp of the מזבח was different: it rose one cubit for every three and a half cubits, plus one and a third fingerbreadths, measured by the thumb.
steps.whatsHappening: רמי בר חמא adds a measurement that closes the earlier discussion about the ramps of the מזבח.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The small ramps had a slope of 1 to 3. The main ramp of the מזבח was a little longer for each cubit of height, so it was slightly less steep. This is a factual measurement, not part of an argument.

keyTerms.meaning: the small ramps
the main ramp of the altar
a cubit (a unit of length)
a fingerbreadth (a small unit of length)
by the thumb measure

steps.whatToRemember: The main ramp of the מזבח was a little less steep than the small ramps.

phrases.english: Rami bar Ḥama says:
All of the small ramps
were three cubits for each cubit,
phrases.notes: He means three cubits of length for every one cubit of height.

phrases.english: except for the ramp of the altar,
which was three and a half cubits
and a fingerbreadth and a third of a fingerbreadth, by the thumb measure.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the earlier discussion of the altar's ramps.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Small ramps had a slope of 1:3. The main altar ramp was 1 cubit of height per 3.5 cubits + 1⅓ fingerbreadths of length.

steps.title: Where meal offerings are handled and eaten
steps.stepSummary: The משנה says that קמיצה of a מנחה may be done anywhere in the עזרה, and that the rest is eaten inside the courtyard by male כהנים, cooked any way, until midnight.
steps.simpleTranslation: The handful could be taken from מנחות anywhere in the עזרה. The rest was eaten inside the curtains, by male כהנים, prepared in any way, during that day and night until midnight.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה gives the basic rules for מנחות: where the handful is taken, and who eats the rest, where and when.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה gives five details: the קמיצה can be done anywhere in the עזרה; the eating must be inside the courtyard; only male כהנים may eat; it may be prepared as any kind of food; and it may be eaten until midnight. The phrase 'anywhere in the עזרה' will lead the גמרא to ask about the היכל.

keyTerms.meaning: meal offering(s)
the priest taking a handful of the flour to burn on the מזבח
the Temple courtyard
the curtains around the courtyard
male כהנים
midnight

steps.confusionAlert: The handful (קמיצה) goes on the מזבח. What is eaten by the כהנים is the leftover flour after the handful is taken.
steps.whyThisMatters: This משנה is the base for the coming גמרא, which asks whether 'anywhere in the עזרה' also includes the היכל.

phrases.english: MISHNA:
Meal offerings had their handful removed
in any place in the Temple courtyard,
and they were eaten inside the curtains,
phrases.notes: The curtains surrounded the courtyard of the משכן, so 'inside the curtains' means inside the courtyard.

phrases.english: by males of the priesthood,
prepared as any kind of food,
for a day and a night, until midnight.

steps.triggerLanguage: מְנָחוֹת הָיוּ נִקְמָצוֹת בְּכׇל מָקוֹם בָּעֲזָרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic: the rules of מנחות.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: קמיצה may be done anywhere in the עזרה. The remainder is eaten in the courtyard by male כהנים, cooked any way, until midnight.

steps.title: A handful taken in the Sanctuary is still valid
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר rules that a מנחה whose קמיצה was done in the היכל is valid, comparing it to the removal of the frankincense bowls (בזיכין).
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר says: if the handful of a מנחה was taken in the היכל, the offering is valid. We see this from the removal of the frankincense bowls, which was done in the היכל.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings רבי אלעזר, who adds that the קמיצה may also be done in the היכל, and not only in the עזרה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The בזיכין of frankincense stood next to the לחם הפנים in the היכל. Removing them works like a קמיצה, since it frees the bread to be eaten. That removal was done in the היכל, so רבי אלעזר says a קמיצה done in the היכל is also valid.

keyTerms.meaning: the Sanctuary, the inner building beyond the courtyard
valid
removing the bowls of frankincense from the שולחן
we have found (a model case to learn from)

phrases.english: GEMARA:
Rabbi Elazar says:
A meal offering whose handful was removed in the Sanctuary is valid,
as we found with the removal of the bowls.
phrases.notes: These are the two bowls of frankincense next to the לחם הפנים on the שולחן, inside the היכל.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר: מִנְחָה שֶׁנִּקְמְצָה בַּהֵיכָל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes beyond the משנה's 'anywhere in the עזרה' and includes the היכל too.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A קמיצה done in the היכל is valid, learned from the removal of the בזיכין.

steps.title: The handful must be taken where a non-priest may stand
steps.stepSummary: רבי ירמיה challenges רבי אלעזר from a ברייתא: 'וקמץ משם' means the קמיצה must be in a place where a זר may stand, which rules out the היכל.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ירמיה objects: the פסוק says 'and he shall take a handful from there.' This means from a place where the feet of a non-כהן stand.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי ירמיה attacks רבי אלעזר's ruling with a ברייתא that seems to say the קמיצה must be done in the courtyard.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'משם' (from there) points back to where the owner, a non-כהן, brings the מנחה. A זר may stand in the עזרה but not in the היכל. So the קמיצה belongs in the עזרה, which seems to contradict רבי אלעזר.

keyTerms.meaning: 'and he shall take a handful from there' (ויקרא 2:2)
a non-כהן

phrases.english: Rabbi Yirmeya raises an objection:
"And he shall take a handful from there":
phrases.notes: ויקרא 2:2

phrases.english: from a place where the feet of the non-priest stand.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Directly challenges רבי אלעזר's ruling in step 3.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אלעזר's ruling that a קמיצה done in the היכל is valid.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא reads 'משם' as a place where a זר may stand. A זר may not enter the היכל, so a קמיצה there should not be valid.

steps.title: Ben Beteira reads 'from there' as fixing a left-handed handful
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא continues: בן בתירא learns from ״מִשָּׁם״ that a קמיצה taken with the left hand must be put back and taken again with the right.
steps.simpleTranslation: בן בתירא says: How do we know that if the כהן took the handful with his left hand, he should put it back and take it again with his right? Because the פסוק says 'from there', meaning from the place he already took it from.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא that רבי ירמיה quoted keeps going. It gives a second, different reading of the word ״מִשָּׁם״, from בן בתירא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first opinion in the ברייתא read ״מִשָּׁם״ as a location: a place where a זר may stand. בן בתירא reads it as 'from the place it was already taken from.' That teaches that a left-handed קמיצה is not the end of the story. The כהן returns the flour to the vessel and does it again properly with his right hand.

keyTerms.meaning: Took a handful (the act of קמיצה from the מנחה)
Left hand / right hand. עבודה must be done with the right.
That he should put it back
The פסוק teaches

steps.confusionAlert: This is still the ברייתא talking, not a new statement of the גמרא. בן בתירא uses the same word ״מִשָּׁם״ for a totally different lesson.

phrases.english: Ben Beteira says:
From where do we know that if he took the handful with the left hand,
he should put it back and take the handful with the right?
The verse says: "from there"
phrases.notes: ויקרא 2:2

phrases.english: meaning from the place where he already took a handful.
phrases.notes: He means: put the flour back into the vessel it came from, and take the handful again.

steps.alternativePossibleLabel: קשיא (still part of the source used to challenge רבי אלעזר)
steps.triggerLanguage: בֶּן בְּתִירָא אוֹמֵר: מִנַּיִן שֶׁאִם קָמַץ בִּשְׂמֹאל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא quoted in step 4 with a second opinion on ״מִשָּׁם״.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A קמיצה taken with the left hand must be returned to the vessel and taken again with the right, learned from ״מִשָּׁם״.

steps.title: The verse only comes to make the whole courtyard valid
steps.stepSummary: The answer to רבי ירמיה's challenge: 'a place where a זר may stand' does not exclude the היכל. It only teaches that every part of the עזרה is valid for קמיצה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say רבי ירמיה himself asked the question and answered it. Others say רבי עקיבא told רבי ירמיה בר תחליפא: Let me explain it to you. The פסוק is needed only to make the entire courtyard valid.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge against רבי אלעזר from step 4. It gives two versions of who gave the answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 4, ״מִשָּׁם״ seemed to mean 'only where a זר stands, and not in the היכל.' The answer flips its purpose. It is an inclusion that makes the whole עזרה valid, not an exclusion that rules out the היכל. So רבי אלעזר's ruling that a קמיצה done in the היכל is valid still stands.

keyTerms.meaning: Raises a challenge ... and resolves it
I will explain it to you
It was needed only for
To make valid
The Temple courtyard

steps.whyThisMatters: This saves רבי אלעזר's ruling. The same words can be read as including the whole courtyard instead of excluding the היכל.

phrases.english: There are those who say:

phrases.aramaic: הוּא מוֹתֵיב לַהּ וְהוּא מְפָרֵק לַהּ;
phrases.english: he raises the challenge and he answers it;
phrases.notes: "He" is רבי ירמיה, who raised the challenge back in step 4.

phrases.english: and there are those who say:

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא לְרַבִּי יִרְמְיָה בַּר תַּחְלִיפָא,
phrases.english: Rabbi Akiva said to Rabbi Yirmeya bar Tachlifa:
I will explain it to you:
it was needed only
to make the entire courtyard, all of it, valid.

steps.triggerLanguage: לֹא נִצְרְכָא אֶלָּא לְהַכְשִׁיר כׇּל הָעֲזָרָה כּוּלָּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 4 against רבי אלעזר (step 3).
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpreting the purpose of the פסוק: an inclusion, not an exclusion
steps.terutzHavaAmina: ״מִשָּׁם״ limits קמיצה to where a זר stands, so the היכל is excluded.
steps.terutzMaskana: ״מִשָּׁם״ only teaches that every part of the עזרה is valid. It says nothing against the היכל.

steps.title: Why we needed that verse: we might have required the north side
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains why the פסוק was needed. We might have compared a מנחה to an עולה, since both are קדשי קדשים, and required the north side.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have thought: an עולה is קדשי קדשים and a מנחה is קדשי קדשים. So just as an עולה must be done in the north, a מנחה must also be done in the north.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא backs up its answer. It shows the mistake we might have made without the פסוק that validates the whole courtyard.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An עולה must be slaughtered in the north (צפון) of the עזרה. Since a מנחה shares the same holiness level, we might have copied that rule over to the קמיצה. The פסוק comes to block that idea and allow the entire עזרה.

keyTerms.meaning: It would have entered your mind to say (the 'I might have thought')
Burnt offering
Meal (flour) offering
Offerings of the highest holiness level
Requires the north side of the courtyard

phrases.english: It would have entered your mind to say:
since a burnt offering is of the most holy offerings,
and a meal offering is of the most holy offerings,
just as a burnt offering requires the north,
so too a meal offering requires the north.

steps.triggerLanguage: סָלְקָא דַּעְתָּךְ אָמֵינָא: הוֹאִיל וְעוֹלָה קׇדְשֵׁי קָדָשִׁים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the need for the teaching given in step 6.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Showing the 'I might have thought' that makes the פסוק necessary
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A מנחה, like an עולה, needs the north side.
steps.terutzMaskana: The פסוק teaches that the whole עזרה is valid for קמיצה.

steps.title: The comparison fails: an עולה is burned completely
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the comparison. An עולה is special because it is כליל, burned completely, so a מנחה cannot be learned from it.
steps.simpleTranslation: What about an עולה? It is special because it is burned completely!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא knocks down the 'I might have thought' from step 7. This reopens the question of why the פסוק was needed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Learning one case from another only works if they are truly alike. An עולה has a stricter feature: the whole thing goes on the מזבח. A מנחה does not have that feature. So the north rule could be tied to that strictness, and we could never have copied it onto a מנחה.

keyTerms.meaning: What about ...? (the standard formula for pointing out a difference)
In that it is (introduces the special feature)
Completely burned on the מזבח

steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא is not taking back the answer from step 6. It is only attacking the reason given for why the פסוק was needed. The search for a better reason continues.

phrases.english: What about a burnt offering?
It is special in that it is completely burned!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the comparison between עולה and מנחה offered in step 7.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Only the comparison used to explain why the פסוק was needed
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: An עולה has a stricter feature (כליל) that a מנחה lacks, so the north rule cannot be carried over.

steps.title: A meal offering cannot be learned from a sin offering
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא considers learning the north-side rule for a מנחה from a חטאת, but rejects it because a חטאת atones for sins punished by כרת.
steps.simpleTranslation: Maybe learn it from a חטאת? No. A חטאת is special because it atones for people who are liable to כרת.
steps.whatsHappening: Having rejected the עולה, the גמרא now tries the חטאת as a model for the מנחה and immediately rejects it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A חטאת is also קדשי קדשים and must be slaughtered in the north, so it looked like a possible source. But a חטאת has a feature a מנחה lacks: it atones for very serious sins that carry כרת. Because of that extra power, its north-side rule cannot be carried over to a מנחה.

keyTerms.meaning: Sin offering, brought for certain sins done by mistake
People who did sins whose punishment is כרת (being cut off)
'What about X? X is special because...': the standard way of rejecting a comparison

phrases.english: From a sin offering? What about a sin offering?
phrases.notes: He means: maybe we could learn that a מנחה needs the north side from a חטאת.

phrases.english: It is special because it atones for those liable to karet!

steps.triggerLanguage: מָה לְחַטָּאת, שֶׁכֵּן מְכַפֶּרֶת עַל חַיָּיבֵי כָרֵיתוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the search for a source after the עולה comparison was rejected in Step 8.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the comparison of מנחה to חטאת for the north-side rule.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: A חטאת atones for sins carrying כרת, a stronger feature that a מנחה does not have.

steps.title: A meal offering cannot be learned from a guilt offering
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא considers learning the north-side rule from an אשם, but rejects it because an אשם is a blood offering and a מנחה is not.
steps.simpleTranslation: Maybe learn it from an אשם? No. An אשם is special because it is a kind of offering made with blood.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries the אשם as a model for the מנחה and rejects it too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An אשם is קדשי קדשים and slaughtered in the north, and it lacks the special features of the עולה and the חטאת. But it is still an animal offering whose main service is done with its blood. A מנחה is flour and has no blood, so the comparison fails.

keyTerms.meaning: Guilt offering
Kinds of blood offerings, animal קרבנות whose service is done with blood

phrases.english: From a guilt offering? What about a guilt offering?
It is special because it is one of the types of blood offerings!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Same pattern as Step 9, now applied to the אשם.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the comparison of מנחה to אשם for the north-side rule.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: An אשם is a blood offering, while a מנחה has no blood.

steps.title: A meal offering cannot be learned from all of them together
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא tries learning from what all these offerings share, but rejects that too, because all of them are blood offerings.
steps.simpleTranslation: Maybe learn it from all of them together? No. They are all special because they are all blood offerings.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא makes one last attempt to combine the עולה, חטאת and אשם into one source, and rejects it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each special feature (כליל, atoning for כרת) belongs to only one offering, so combining them gets past those. But one feature is shared by all of them: they are all blood offerings. A מנחה does not have it, so even the combined comparison fails. This shows we never would have thought a מנחה needs the north, which brings back the question of why the פסוק was needed.

keyTerms.meaning: From all of them: learning from what several sources have in common

steps.whatToRemember: No animal קרבן can serve as a model for a מנחה needing the north side, because every one of them is a blood offering and a מנחה is not.

phrases.english: From all of them? What about all of them?
phrases.notes: He means the עולה, חטאת and אשם together.

phrases.english: They are special because they are types of blood offerings!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the series of comparisons from Steps 8 to 10 by rejecting a combined comparison.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects learning the north-side rule for a מנחה from all the north-side offerings together.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: All of them share being blood offerings, which a מנחה is not.

steps.title: A new reason the verse was needed: the meal offering is brought to the altar
steps.stepSummary: Since no comparison works, the גמרא gives a different reason the פסוק was needed. The פסוקים say the מנחה is brought to the מזבח and the קמיצה is taken from it, so we might have thought the קמיצה must be done by the מזבח.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, the פסוק was needed. You might have thought that since it says 'And he shall bring it to the altar' and then 'And he shall take up from it his handful'...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is starting a new answer to why the ברייתא needed a פסוק. This line sets up a mistaken idea, and the rest of the thought continues in the next lines.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The idea that a מנחה is like the north-side animal offerings has failed, so the גמרא looks for a different mistake the פסוק prevents. The פסוקים first describe bringing the מנחה near the מזבח, then the קמיצה. Read together, they could suggest the קמיצה must happen at that spot by the מזבח, and the פסוק 'וקמץ משם' would then teach that anywhere in the עזרה is fine.

keyTerms.meaning: It was needed: the reason a פסוק or teaching is not extra
You might have thought: introduces a mistaken first idea
Bringing the מנחה near the corner of the מזבח
The handful taken from the מנחה and burned on the מזבח

steps.confusionAlert: This is not the final answer yet. The גמרא is only explaining what we might have wrongly thought; the sentence ends in a dash and finishes in the next lines.

phrases.english: Rather, it was necessary;
it could enter your mind to say,
since it is written:
“And he shall bring it to the altar,”
phrases.notes: ויקרא 2:8

phrases.english: “And he shall take up from it his handful” –
phrases.notes: ויקרא 6:8

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the failed reason from Steps 7 to 11 with a new reason for why the פסוק was needed.
steps.terutzResolutionType: New reason why the פסוק was needed (איצטריך), based on reading two פסוקים together
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Because the מנחה is brought to the מזבח and then the קמיצה is taken from it, one might think the קמיצה must be done at the spot by the מזבח.
steps.terutzMaskana: The פסוק teaches that the קמיצה is valid anywhere in the עזרה. Step 13 finishes the explanation.

steps.title: We might have linked the handful-taking to the southwest corner
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes its answer. Without the פסוק, we might have thought that the קמיצה, like the הגשה, must be done at the southwest corner of the מזבח. The פסוק teaches us otherwise.
steps.simpleTranslation: Just as the bringing-near of the מנחה is done at the southwest corner of the מזבח, so too the taking of the handful would have to be done at the southwest corner. That is why the פסוק was needed, to teach us otherwise.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא completes the answer it began in the previous step. It spells out the mistake we might have made, and says the פסוק comes to block that mistake.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוקים put the הגשה, which is done at the southwest corner, right next to the קמיצה. So we might have tied the two together and required the קמיצה at that exact corner too. The phrase קא משמע לן means the פסוק is there to tell us this link is wrong.

keyTerms.meaning: Bringing the מנחה near to the מזבח
The כהן taking a handful of flour from the מנחה
The southwest corner of the מזבח
"It teaches us". The text comes to tell us something we would not have known

steps.whatToRemember: The פסוק about the מנחה is needed so that we do not require the קמיצה at the southwest corner of the מזבח, the way the הגשה is done there.

phrases.english: Just as the bringing-near is at the southwest corner,
so too the taking of the handful would be at the southwest corner;
so it teaches us [otherwise].
phrases.notes: The פסוק is there to teach us that the קמיצה does not have to be done at that corner.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the answer begun in Step 12 by spelling out the mistaken idea the פסוק blocks.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Identifies a mistaken idea that the פסוק is needed to rule out
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The קמיצה must be done at the southwest corner of the מזבח, like the הגשה.
steps.terutzMaskana: The פסוק teaches that the קמיצה is not tied to the southwest corner.

steps.title: Peace offerings slaughtered in the Sanctuary are valid
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן rules that שלמים slaughtered inside the היכל are כשרים. The less holy courtyard, where they are normally slaughtered, should not be stricter than the holier היכל.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן says: שלמים that someone slaughtered in the היכל are valid. The פסוק says, "And he shall slaughter it at the entrance of the אהל מועד," which means the courtyard. And the less important place should not be stricter than the main, holier place.
steps.whatsHappening: A new topic begins. רבי יוחנן states a rule: שלמים slaughtered inside the היכל are still valid.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Torah says to slaughter שלמים "at the entrance of the אהל מועד," meaning the courtyard. The היכל is holier than the courtyard. If slaughtering in the less holy place works, slaughtering in the holier place should surely work too. This reasoning is called לא יהא טפל חמור מן העיקר.

keyTerms.meaning: Peace offerings
The Sanctuary, the holy building inside the courtyard
Secondary, the less important thing
Primary, the main and more important thing
Valid

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the עזרה (courtyard) and the היכל (the building inside it). In this rule the courtyard is the "secondary" place, and the היכל is the "primary," holier place.
steps.whyThisMatters: The rest of this section tests whether this "less holy can't be stricter" logic really holds up.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yoḥanan says:
Peace offerings that one slaughtered in the Sanctuary are valid,
as it is stated: "And he shall slaughter it at the entrance of the Tent of Meeting" (the courtyard),
phrases.notes: ויקרא 3:2. Some versions leave out the word in round brackets.

phrases.aramaic: וְלֹא יְהֵא טָפֵל חָמוּר מִן הָעִיקָּר.
phrases.english: and the secondary place should not be stricter than the primary place.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new statement that parallels רבי אלעזר's ruling in step 3. There, a קמיצה done in the היכל is valid; here, שלמים slaughtered in the היכל are valid.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: שלמים slaughtered in the היכל are כשרים, based on the פסוק and the logic that the courtyard cannot be stricter than the היכל.

steps.title: A ברייתא about eating holy offerings in the Sanctuary during danger
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to challenge רבי יוחנן. רבי יוחנן בן בתירה uses a special פסוק to allow כהנים to eat קדשי קדשים in the היכל when gentiles surround the courtyard.
steps.simpleTranslation: They raised an objection: רבי יוחנן בן בתירה says, from where do we know that if gentiles surrounded the whole courtyard, the כהנים may go in there and eat קדשי קדשים there? The פסוק says, "In a most holy place shall you eat it."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a ברייתא that it will use to challenge רבי יוחנן. This step sets up the challenge, and the actual attack comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא says that, in an emergency, כהנים may eat קדשי קדשים in the היכל. It learns this from a special פסוק. The point to notice is that the ברייתא felt it needed a פסוק for this at all.

keyTerms.meaning: The Temple courtyard
The most holy offerings, which are normally eaten in the courtyard
"The פסוק says". Introduces the source

phrases.english: They raised an objection:
Rabbi Yoḥanan ben Beteira says:

phrases.aramaic: מִנַּיִן שֶׁאִם הִקִּיפוּ גּוֹיִם אֶת כׇּל הָעֲזָרָה –
phrases.english: From where do we know that if gentiles surrounded the entire courtyard,
the priests may enter there,
phrases.notes: "There" means the היכל, the building inside the courtyard.

phrases.english: and eat the most holy offerings there?
The verse states: "In a most holy place shall you eat it."
phrases.notes: במדבר 18:10

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a ברייתא to set up a challenge against רבי יוחנן's rule in Step 14.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's rule that the היכל cannot be stricter than the courtyard
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא needs a special פסוק to allow eating in the היכל. That suggests the "less holy can't be stricter" logic is not enough on its own. The attack is spelled out in the next step.

steps.title: Why does the ברייתא need a special verse?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא presses the challenge. Why did the ברייתא need a special פסוק? It could have used רבי יוחנן's logic: if the food may be eaten in the courtyard, surely it may be eaten in the holier היכל.
steps.simpleTranslation: And why is a special פסוק needed? Let us say: "In the courtyard of the אהל מועד they shall eat it," and the less important place should not be stricter than the main place!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא spells out its challenge to רבי יוחנן. If his reasoning were correct, the ברייתא would not have needed a special פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Torah says קדשי קדשים are eaten in the courtyard. By רבי יוחנן's logic, eating them in the holier היכל should be allowed automatically. But the ברייתא brought a separate פסוק instead. That suggests רבי יוחנן's kind of reasoning is not accepted.

keyTerms.meaning: "But why?" Introduces a challenge
"Let us say". Suggests a different way to learn the law
Stricter, more severe

steps.whatToRemember: The challenge: if "the less holy place can't be stricter than the holier one" were valid reasoning, the ברייתא would not need a special פסוק to allow eating in the היכל.

phrases.english: But why? Let us say:
"In the court of the Tent of Meeting they shall eat it,"
phrases.notes: ויקרא 6:9

phrases.aramaic: וְלֹא יְהֵא טָפֵל חָמוּר מִן הָעִיקָּר!
phrases.english: and the secondary place should not be stricter than the primary place!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the ברייתא from Step 15 to directly attack רבי יוחנן's reasoning in Step 14.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's reasoning of לא יהא טפל חמור מן העיקר
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If that reasoning worked, eating in the היכל would follow automatically from eating in the courtyard. The ברייתא's need for a separate פסוק shows the reasoning is not relied on.

steps.title: Serving before the Master is different from eating before Him
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the comparison. Service may be done in the master's presence, so the 'secondary should not be stricter' logic works for slaughtering. Eating is not done in the master's presence, so that logic does not work, and a פסוק was needed.
steps.simpleTranslation: How can you compare them? Slaughtering is service, and a servant serves right in front of his master, so we say the courtyard cannot be stricter than the היכל. Eating is different, because a servant does not eat in front of his master, so we do not use that logic. That is why the ברייתא needed a פסוק.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רבי יוחנן. His logic works for slaughtering but not for eating, so the ברייתא really did need a פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule 'the secondary should not be stricter than the primary' only works where the holier place suits the activity. Service belongs in the master's presence, so the holier היכל is even better for it. Eating in front of the master is not respectful, so being holier does not make the היכל better for eating.

keyTerms.meaning: How can you compare? (rejects a comparison)
Sacrificial service
In the presence of his master
The secondary, less holy place (the courtyard)
The primary, holier place (the היכל)

steps.whatToRemember: The 'secondary should not be stricter than the primary' logic works for service, which suits the master's presence. It does not work for eating, which does not.
steps.whyThisMatters: This answer keeps רבי יוחנן's ruling that שלמים slaughtered in the היכל are כשרים, and it also explains why eating in the היכל needed a פסוק.

phrases.english: How can these be compared?!
There, it is a sacrificial service,
phrases.notes: "There" means רבי יוחנן's case of slaughtering שלמים.

phrases.english: and a person serves in the presence of his master,
phrases.notes: The master is ה׳. The היכל is the place closest to His presence.

phrases.english: so we say: the secondary should not be
stricter than the primary.
But eating,
where a person does not eat in the presence of his master,

phrases.aramaic: לֹא יְהֵא טָפֵל חָמוּר מִן הָעִיקָּר –
phrases.english: 'the secondary should not be stricter than the primary'
we do not say.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 16 by showing that slaughtering and eating are not alike.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: One might think that if the courtyard's lower holiness allows eating, the holier היכל would surely allow it too, so no פסוק would be needed.
steps.terutzMaskana: The קל וחומר works only for service, which suits the master's presence. Eating does not, so a פסוק was needed. רבי יוחנן's ruling stands.

steps.title: The bird sin offering belongs at the southwest corner
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה teaches that the חטאת העוף is done at the southwest corner of the מזבח. It is כשר anywhere on the מזבח, but that corner is its proper place.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: The bird sin offering was done at the southwest corner. It was valid anywhere, but this was its proper place.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It gives the proper place on the מזבח for the חטאת העוף.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה separates the ideal place from what is needed after the fact. The southwest corner is where it should be done from the start, but doing it elsewhere on the מזבח does not make it פסול.

keyTerms.meaning: משנה (short for מַתְנִיתִין)
A bird sin offering
The southwest corner of the מזבח
Valid

phrases.english: MISHNA:
The bird sin offering would be performed
at the southwest corner;
and in any place it was valid,
phrases.notes: He means any place on the מזבח.

phrases.english: but this was its place.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ חַטַּאת הָעוֹף הָיְתָה נַעֲשֵׂית עַל קֶרֶן דְּרוֹמִית מַעֲרָבִית
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה after the previous discussion ended.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The חטאת העוף should be done at the southwest corner, but it is כשר anywhere on the מזבח.

steps.title: Three rites done on the lower part of the southwest corner
steps.stepSummary: The משנה says the southwest corner serves three rites below and three above. The lower three are the חטאת העוף, the הגשות of מנחות, and pouring out the leftover blood.
steps.simpleTranslation: That corner was used for three things below and three things above. Below: the bird sin offering, bringing meal offerings near the מזבח, and pouring out the leftover blood.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה says the southwest corner has three uses below and three above. It then lists the three below.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The corner is divided into lower and upper sections, and each section has its own rites. The הגשות listed here are the same southwest-corner הגשה mentioned back in step 13.

keyTerms.meaning: Below (the lower part of the מזבח)
Bringing מנחות near the מזבח
The leftover blood poured out at the base

phrases.english: And for three matters that corner
would serve below,
phrases.notes: Below and above mean below and above the red line that ran around the middle of the מזבח.

phrases.english: and for three above.
Below: the bird sin offering,
and the bringing near of meal offerings, and the remaining blood.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּשְׁלֹשָׁה דְּבָרִים הָיְתָה אוֹתָהּ קֶרֶן מְשַׁמֶּשֶׁת מִלְּמַטָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Expands on the southwest corner from step 18 by listing all of its uses.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The lower part of the southwest corner is used for the חטאת העוף, the הגשות, and the leftover blood.

steps.title: Three rites done on the upper part of the southwest corner
steps.stepSummary: The upper three rites are the wine libation, the water libation, and the עולת העוף when there are too many to do in the east.
steps.simpleTranslation: Above: the wine libation, the water libation, and the bird burnt offering when there are too many of them in the east.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה finishes its list. These are the three rites done on the upper part of the southwest corner.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The עולת העוף is normally done at the southeast corner. The southwest corner is only a backup when too many birds are waiting there.

keyTerms.meaning: Pouring the wine libation
The water libation (on סוכות)
A bird burnt offering
Numerous, too many

steps.whatToRemember: The southwest corner has six jobs. Below: חטאת העוף, הגשות, leftover blood. Above: wine, water, and extra עולות העוף.

phrases.english: And above: the wine libation,
and the water, and the bird burnt offering
phrases.notes: The water is the special water libation poured on סוכות.

phrases.english: when it is too numerous in the east.
phrases.notes: "The east" is the southeast corner, where bird burnt offerings are usually done.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the list that step 19 began, now giving the three upper rites.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The upper part of the southwest corner is used for the wine and water libations, and for the עולת העוף when there is overflow.

steps.title: Everyone goes up the ramp on the right side
steps.stepSummary: The משנה begins a new rule: everyone who goes up to the מזבח goes up by the right side of the ramp.
steps.simpleTranslation: All who go up to the מזבח go up by way of the right side.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה moves to a new rule about how the כהנים walk up the ramp to the מזבח. The sentence continues in the next section.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the start of a rule about the direction of movement on the ramp. Going up is on the right side. The details are given as the משנה continues.

keyTerms.meaning: Those who go up to the מזבח
By way of the right side

phrases.english: All who ascend to the altar
ascend by way of the right,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the corners of the מזבח to how the כהנים walk up the ramp.
